NUEVO LAREDO, Tamaulipas — More than 100 people have been helped so far by Piso Firme 2026, the Nuevo Laredo municipal program that replaces dirt floors with concrete in family homes — and the city says applications are still open, with spots still available.

The program, pushed by Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, targets families whose homes still have packed-earth floors, framing the work as a basic-needs effort that starts inside the home and lifts living conditions from there, according to CML Noticias, which reported on the municipal announcement.

To apply, residents must bring: an entry application to the social program, a copy of a valid INE voter ID, an updated CURP, a current water bill, a current property-tax (predial) receipt, proof of ownership such as a title or purchase agreement, a 6x4-inch photo of the front of the home, and a contact phone number. The home must be occupied and have solid walls — block, brick or similar.

Applications are reviewed for compliance with the requirements, and selected applicants are notified. Paperwork is accepted Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM, at the Secretaría de Bienestar Social, in the annex building of the Presidencia Municipal, entering on Maclovio Herrera in colonia Ojo Caliente. More information is available at 867 711 3585 or in person at the service module.

Sources: CML Noticias reporting on the Gobierno Municipal de Nuevo Laredo announcement (Oct. 22, 2026).

title: Nuevo Laredo keeps 'Piso Firme 2026' open: concrete floors for families still living on dirt
